spec.title: codkit PROP-011: CI and the air-gapped circuit

status.comment: standalone CI and air-gapped contract with separate tool, patch-set and fork roots

contract.title: 1. The job contract (the same for any CI)

facts.JOB-CHECKOUT-PATCHSET: checkout of the patch set by the regular CI step;
facts.JOB-PROVIDE-TREE: the fork tree is provided in any way: a bind mount of a persistent directory, a CI volume or cache, an image layer, a checkout as a second repository;
facts.JOB-RUN-CONTAINER: the container is started with three independent paths: the installed toolRoot, the patch set through `--patches-dir`/`CODKIT_PATCHES_DIR`, the fork through `--fork-dir`/`CODKIT_FORK_DIR`;
facts.JOB-ONE-COMMAND: one command, `codkit ci`. The image contains the Codkit runtime and the Node/git/git-lfs environment, but contains no consumer patch set and no fork checkout.

p.AIRGAP-IS-PRIMARY: **The air-gapped circuit is the primary mode, not a degradation**: there is no external internet in the target environment; everything needed is brought in by the supply kit (§7); the customer's CI is any of them (Jenkins/GitHub/GitLab/their own). Every new codkit mechanism is designed for offline first.

p.ZERO-NET-IN-CI: The global `--ci` is a hard zero-network mode: codkit performs no network call at all. The `gitx` module takes `netAllowed`; with `netAllowed=false`, `fetch|clone|pull|lfs pull|push|ls-remote` are not started at all (exit 2 `CK-E-NET-FORBIDDEN` with a text saying which external action the CI has to perform). `publish` is not `--ci`: it refuses the combination with `--ci`, requires `--yes-i-am-publish-bot` and only then turns the network on. Before any materialization or change of refs the publish bot must pass the read-only gate `git ls-remote <publishRemoteUrl>`; a failure ends the command with code 2 and no mutations. Push stays with `publish` alone, on the supplier side. Automated tests: `ci` on the polygon with the network physically off; separately, publish against a local bare remote with the gate checked.

facts.PROFILE-VERIFY: `verify` (the threshold of every PR; seconds to minutes): `check-tree` → the fresh pass → apply → `verify` (PROP-007 §11) → the race guards: the pin guard (the pin of the PR branch equals the pin of the target branch; in CI the `codkit.json` of the PR is compared against base) - a mismatch → 1 with the hint `codkit rebase-onto-pin`.
facts.PROFILE-BUILD: `build`: `verify` + the dependencies (the upstream fast path by the hash of the manifests; on a lock change, a full install from the internal registry) + `build up` + `build errors` (one pass, full output) + own tests + contract tests; the upstream hygiene/eslint run BEFORE the materialization of the overlay targets upstream is strict about (the order: hygiene → overlay apply → our checks). The skeleton and the order are universal; the scripts each step runs are the project type's answer (VS Code type: `spec://codkit/modules/vscode/PROP-004#VSCODE-BUILD-STEPS`).
facts.CI-PIN-GUARD-BASE-FLAG: The CI itself names the base for the pin guard: the flag `--pin-guard-base <ref>` (a ref in the patch-set repository; the `codkit.json` of the patch-set work tree and the one at the ref are compared). Without the flag the step is skipped with an info line - the run does not pretend that the guard passed. On a mismatch the hint points at the implemented `rebase-onto-pin` command.
facts.CI-DEPS-POLICY-M1: The M1 decision on «on a lock change, a full install from the internal registry»: **`ci` installs nothing itself** - installing the dependencies from the internal registry is a job step OUTSIDE the codkit container (or a pre-filled cache/mount). The behaviour of `ci --profile build`: the npm receipts `node_modules/.package-lock.json` and `build/node_modules/.package-lock.json` of the tree are absent (including the case of an empty bind-mount directory left behind) → exit 2 `CK-E-DEPS-MISSING` with the text «provide node_modules via cache/mount (air-gapped supply kit)»; a stale `.codkit/build/deps-hash.json` does not cancel this presence probe; the lock or `.nvmrc` changed against the record → the warning «refresh node_modules out of band», the run continues and the record is updated (the warning fires once per lock change, not forever); the record is one per tree, keyed by `treeId` (like the daemon records).
facts.CACHE-KEY-RULE: The cache: the key is `pin.sha` plus the hash of the lock files; the only writer is the job of the main branch, the rest read. A toolchain change (the cycle advisory) changes the key, that is, a controlled full rebuild. The cold build (~an hour) is paid once per agent/cache.

fresh.title: 4. The «from scratch» pass and the cleanup whitelist

p.FRESH-SEMANTICS: «From scratch» refers to the content of the tree: the tracked files are brought to the pin by a git checkout (only the changed files are rewritten - together with the mtime discipline this keeps incremental compilation warm), then the delta is applied. Untracked content is cleaned **by a whitelist** that deliberately keeps the build caches.

p.CLEANUP-WHITELIST-CONTENT: `cleanupWhitelist` (the conventions of PROP-003 §3), the pattern semantics are gitignore-style; refined by the M0 implementation: `node_modules/` (at any level), `.build/`, `/out*/` (anchored: the top level only - an unanchored `out*/` would protect `outer/` and `output/` anywhere as well), `extensions/*/out/`, `extensions/*/dist/`, `.eslintcache`, `*.tsbuildinfo`; the `.git/codkit/` entry of the early edition is removed - git does not report the content of `.git` in the untracked list, and the mark is untouchable anyway. In addition, the own directory `src/vs/<ownDirName>/` and `.git/**` are always kept. The algorithm: `git clean -fdx` is NOT used; the untracked list is the union of `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` and `… --others --ignored --exclude-standard` (a lone `--others` does NOT show ignored files), by files (without `--directory` - otherwise a collapsed directory would delete the whitelisted content inside it); the entries covered by the whitelist are subtracted from it, and the rest is deleted. The discipline: what is not in the list is deleted. The pattern semantics, the algorithm and the discipline are the engine's; **which** paths a build leaves behind is the project type's answer (VS Code type: `spec://codkit/modules/vscode/PROP-002#VSCODE-CLEANUP-WHITELIST`), and the list above is that type's value carried here until the extraction of phase P2.

p.DEPS-FAST-PATH: Installing the tree dependencies after a restore relies on the upstream fast path «the dependencies are up to date» (the hash of the manifests, the lock and `.nvmrc`) - seconds when the lock files are unchanged.

p.SAFE-DIRECTORY-RULE: A mounted tree usually belongs to another uid: before the first git call, `ci` checks for the «dubious ownership» sign (a trial `git status`; the characteristic error) and adds both paths to the configuration of the **container**: for this `ci` uses not `/dev/null` but the file `.codkit/gitconfig-ci` (pointed at through `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` inside the container) with the entries `safe.directory=<tree>` and `<patchset>` - without touching the machine. The right to write into the tree and into the cache directories is checked before the work starts. Agreeing the uid/gid is the contract of starting the container (the documentation of PROP-012 §4).

p.SAFE-DIRECTORY-IMPL: The M1 implementation: `gitx` gained the option `gitConfigGlobal` (it replaces `/dev/null`; the system configuration stays off) and a run-wide setting - ONLY a `ci` run uses it, and only after the probe has fired; `.codkit/gitconfig-ci` is created or extended with the union of the safe.directory entries (the tree + the patch set). The write probes: the tree is checked (check-tree in write mode); the patch-set runtime is checked by actually creating the lock before any work with the tree, and `EACCES`/`EPERM`/`EROFS` are turned into exit 2 `CK-E-TREE-READONLY` with a hint about a separate writable `.codkit` mount. The dubious-ownership branch is confirmed by a live Docker matrix with owner 1000 and process UID 10001; the unit tests cover the writer/gitx and the classification of the lock I/O.

p.EFFECTIVE-DIFF-RULE: For a PR the CI builds the diff of the **applied states**: the tip of the generated branch for base and for the PR (`git diff base-top pr-top` in the tree) - this is an ordinary code diff, which the reviewer reads instead of a diff of patch files; plus the inventory diff (`inventory --diff`). It is implemented inside `ci --profile verify` by the flag `--effective-diff <base-ref>`; the output is a CI file artifact.

p.EFFECTIVE-DIFF-IMPL: The M1 implementation: the base tip is built by `syncEngine.buildAppliedTip()` - the generated commits of the base state are written into the object database of the TREE without touching the working copy, the refs, the mark or the cache (for a disposable ci tree this is normal; for a live tree it would be a surprise - hence only in `ci`). The requirements: the base pin is reachable in the tree AND the base delta applies on its own pin; otherwise only the inventory diff is built, with a warning (the exit code does not change). The artifacts: `.codkit/out/effective-diff.patch` (the full diff; `--stat` is printed to the output) and `.codkit/out/inventory-diff.md`. The REPAIR-006 refinement (the obsolete M1 text is removed): the base tip is built by `buildGeneratedTip()` - the full generated history, INCLUDING the aggregate own commit of its own (`commitOwn`, PROP-005 LT-OWN; the same layer order as the PR tip), so own files enter the diff of the tips as ordinary code; the literal review of `delta/own/**` in a patch-set PR stays available, but is no longer the only window into own code.

td.SK-FORK-REPO: The fork repository (an upstream mirror + the generated refs)

tr.td: a one-off bundle or mirror into the internal hosting; after that the whole history is inside

td.SK-TREE-NPM: The npm dependencies of the fork tree (60+ directories)

tr.td: the internal registry (overridden at the level of the environment or the user npmrc; the upstream `.npmrc` files are not patched without need)

td.SK-CODKIT-NPM: The npm dependencies of the installed Codkit (`toolRoot/npm-shrinkwrap.json`)

tr.td: the internal registry while the image is built, or a pre-filled `toolRoot/node_modules`; the patch set is independent of these dependencies

td.SK-ELECTRON: The headers and binaries of Electron and Node

tr.td: internal feeds: the regular artifact-feed keys in `product.json` are set by our overlay; or a pre-filled `.build/` in the cache
the `vsix` field of the entry (the regular path) or a pre-filled `.build/builtInExtensions`

p.SUPPLY-KIT-MAINTENANCE: Keeping the table current is an item of the cycle advisory; the external network exists on the supplier side only: the mirror bot (fetch from upstream → push to the mirror) and the publish bot, each with its own service account.

wrapper-examples.title: 8. Wrapper examples (ours, illustrative)
wrapper-examples.fence: FROM node:24-bookworm RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends git git-lfs \ && git lfs install --system && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* COPY . /opt/codkit RUN cd /opt/codkit && npm ci --offline ENTRYPOINT ["/opt/codkit/bin/codkit"]

p.wrapper-run: The run: `docker run --rm --network none -v "$PATCHES":/work/patches -v "$FORK":/work/fork -e CODKIT_PATCHES_DIR=/work/patches -e CODKIT_FORK_DIR=/work/fork codkit-ci ci --profile verify`. Real wrappers must preserve the disjoint-root invariant.

p.WRAPPER-FULL-EXAMPLES: The shapes of the harnesses: a Jenkinsfile - a stage that checks out the patch set → a stage that checks out or mounts the tree (a reference object cache on the agent) → a stage `docker run … codkit ci`; GitHub Actions - two `actions/checkout` steps (the second one the fork repository, `fetch-depth: 0`) → a `docker run …` step. The full example files are placed into `docs/codkit/ci-examples/` at implementation time (without secrets; credentials are the territory of the CI).
